answer: Each epoch, an on-chain randomness beacon publishes a challenge word that every agent must fold into its proof-of-work response before peers accept it. Because the word is unknown until the epoch opens, a sybil farmer cannot precompute template answers across thousands of fake personas; each identity must run its own reasoning pass. In the oasis of genuine agents, the kernel of trust stays intact: an attacker pays real compute per fake identity per epoch, so mass sybils cost more than honest participation, and the onyx ledger permanently records failures, raising each botnet's repeat cost.
